A.biggest_strength: Exploring cross-domain lookup scenarios (e.g., showing how a lookup for www.google.com benefits from a cached .com TLD record) alongside thorough supplementary reference tables.
A.biggest_weakness: Significant factual inaccuracies regarding example.com (attributing it to Cloudflare nameservers and IPs), compounded by massive dead template code and cramped mobile sequence-diagram lifelines.
factual_errors: A claims the authoritative nameserver for example.com is hera.ns.cloudflare.com (108.162.192.162) and its address is 104.20.23.154 with a 300s TTL. In reality, example.com is an IANA-managed domain delegated to a.iana-servers.net and b.iana-servers.net resolving to 93.184.215.14.
The caption claims the records, TTLs, and glue addresses were captured with 'dig +norecurse' for example.com on 16 Oct 2026 and directs the reader to run a nonexistent 'node model.mjs --dig' script.

B.biggest_strength: Flawlessly accurate DNS modeling and packet structures paired with intuitive visual mechanisms—especially the 'SKIPPED: CACHED' badges, decremented TTL returns, and side-by-side wire-latency comparison bars.
B.biggest_weakness: Focuses strictly on subsequent lookups of www.example.com rather than letting students test sibling domains under the same .com TLD.
